correctness.rationale: For every real q in [0,1/2] the principal h_q(z)=z+q log(1+z) has Re h_q' >0, so is univalent; the explicit boundary imaginary-strip bound |Im h_q|<3/2<π/2 makes exp∘h_q univalent with positive real part. The logarithmic image has largest centered Euclidean disk of radius 1+q log 2: the integral Re(h_q(z)/z)>=1+q log2 supplies the Rouché lower disk and the negative real boundary point −1−q log2 supplies upper support. Thus the exponential generator is subordinate to every interpolant and S_0⊂S_q. Positive Taylor coefficients in −h_q(−z) give max_|z|=r |h_q(z)| = r−q log(1−r), so reverse r-dilation is equivalent to r−q log(1−r)≤1. Equality has unique solution R_q=1−qW(1/q) and the canonical extremal for the q=0 target fails for r>R_q; q=0 limit and q=1/2 endpoint are treated separately. Expansion of W gives stated small-q logarithmic-logarithmic asymptotic. Independent decimal bisection q=1/2,1/4,1/8 checked root residuals, not all q.
residual_risks: Exponential injectivity depends on the strict imaginary strip and choice of principal logarithm; this was checked using q≤1/2, not extended beyond this range.
Numerical boundary angular mesh in bundled script is diagnostic only; continuum inequality derives analytically.

value.rationale: The all-q family interpolates between naturally used exponential and apple-like starlike classes, so exactly distinguishing forward from reverse inclusion is a motivated geometric-function problem. The sharp continuum threshold, exact logarithmic inradius, explicit extremal, and singular q→0 asymptotics add nontrivial analytic information beyond coefficient bounds; this is not an arbitrary slice or normalization check.
